text: Tonight, much of the world is reading one headline.
On November nineteenth, in Shenzhen, the leaders of the United States, China and Russia met together, for the first time.
Donald Trump. Xi Jinping. Vladimir Putin. "We're making history," Trump said.
Their joint peace declaration backs stable energy flows, a dialogue on nuclear risks, and strategic stability. And it warns international courts not to abuse their positions.
What it left out: no timetable for arms control talks. And, reports say, no word on the war in Ukraine.
Xi Jinping put it plainly: "Nuclear war cannot be won, and must not be fought."
For billions watching, from cafes to container ports, one question remains: will these words become action?
"No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities," Trump said. The world will be the judge.
